newsitem.title: TURKEY: LEADING TURKISH BANKS CUT LIRA DEPOSIT RATES.
newsitem.headline: LEADING TURKISH BANKS CUT LIRA DEPOSIT RATES.

text.p: Turkey's leading private and state banks cut their lira deposit rates by five points in all maturities following a similar move by small and medium banks, in line with the downward trend in the bond and money markets.

In a joint action, three biggest private banks -- Turkiye Is Bankasi, Yapi ve Kredi Bankasi and Pamukbank -- reduced their one, three and six-month and one-year deposit interest rates by five points to 70, 75, 85 and 90 percent, respectively.
State-run Vakiflar Bank also lowered its deposit rates in all maturities by five points to 64, 71, 77 and 84 percent, respectively.
All of the new rates will be effective from Tuesday.

Small and medium banks had already cut their deposit rates by between one and 10 points last week, following a sharp drop in bond yields, lower money market rates and lower inflation expectations since the beginning of 1997.

After the cuts, banks' rates fell to a range at between 70-75 percent for one-month deposits, 75-80 percent for three-month deposits, 85-90 percent for six-month deposits and 90-95 percent for one-year deposits.

T-bill and bond yields continued their downtrend which began in late December after the government decided to raise withholding tax on interest income from state papers to 12 percent from 10 and delayed the introduction of income tax on interest income from state securities for private investors.
Bond market yields have plunged by more than 25 points since then to around 85 percent.
Some Turkish banks also lowered their interest rates on commercial deposits to below 100 percent and their loan rates by a few points last week.
